column12: Judgement on the comparator. Seltorexant's setting is the adjunctive-MDD slot that atypical antipsychotics hold, and J&J ran it head to head against quetiapine XR in that slot (NCT04513912, NCT03321526). Caplyta is J&J's own brand in that slot, with an adjunctive-MDD label from 6 November 2025 (J&J release; the date was checked by the second reader of the LLY brenipatide seed). Cross-check: Vraylar, the book's anchor for brenipatide in the same disease, reads $9,662 (lookup.py demand Vraylar, Part D 2024), 3% lower. The case against: Caplyta's 2024 Medicare spend is schizophrenia and bipolar depression use, before its MDD label. Per-beneficiary spend covers part of a year, so it understates an annual price. The orexin class sells for far less: Belsomra reads $1,948 per beneficiary (Part D 2024), and Auvelity, the newest MDD-only brand, $4,686. Payers may also put generic quetiapine and aripiprazole first. No list price for seltorexant has been published, since it is not approved

column11: Three filters, applied to the NSDUH past-year MDE pool. (1) Treated: 61.0% of US adults with a past-year MDE received treatment (NIMH, nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression, NSDUH 2021), the book's brenipatide value. (2) Inadequate response to an SSRI: 47% responded (50% or more QIDS-SR reduction) to citalopram in STAR*D level 1 among 2,876 US outpatients, so 53% did not (Trivedi et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28, PMID 16390886). (3) Insomnia symptoms: 'approximately 60 percent of MDD patients on standard-of-care oral antidepressants experience residual insomnia symptoms' (J&J MDD3001 release, 2024-05-29, jnj.com/media-center/press-releases/johnson-johnson-pivotal-study-of-seltorexant-shows-statistically-significant-and-clinically-meaningful-improvement-in-depressive-symptoms-and-sleep-disturbance-outcomes). 0.61 x 0.53 x 0.60 = 0.19398
column12: Judgement: the filters are taken as independent. The label population follows the Phase 3 entry criteria: MDD with insomnia symptoms and an inadequate response to an ongoing SSRI/SNRI (NCT04533529 and NCT06559306 titles; NCT03321526 enrolled inadequate response to 1-3 SSRIs/SNRIs). The case for higher: insomnia is more common in non-responders than the 60% across all treated patients. STAR*D found some insomnia symptom in 84.7% of 3,743 outpatients at baseline, of any severity (Sunderajan et al., CNS Spectr 2010;15(6):394-404, doi:10.1017/s1092852900029266, PMID 20625372). A monotherapy label (NCT07573176) would also drop filter (2). The case for lower: the 60% is J&J's own figure, not a paper, and the trials require moderate-to-severe insomnia. 'Treated' also includes talk therapy alone, while the label needs an ongoing SSRI/SNRI. Filters (2) and (3) cut deeper into the one MDD pool the book carries, so the seltorexant and brenipatide labels overlap only in part

column11: Auvelity, as measured in the book's brenipatide seed (second-reader corrected): 16,448 Part D beneficiaries in 2024 and 9,268 in 2023 (lookup.py demand Auvelity). New patients in 2024 = 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186, over a Medicare pool of 53.1mm Part D enrollees (KFF 2024) x 17.54% with depressive disorders (CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse, 2022) = 9,313,740, less 9,268 = 0.1417%
column12: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity, the newest oral MDD brand with a clean CMS series. It applies the rate Auvelity took of its own label pool (all diagnosed MDD) to seltorexant's narrower label pool. At peak that is 21,414,000 x 0.19398 x 0.001417 = about 5,900 new patients a year. The case for higher: if seltorexant won as many patients as Auvelity in absolute terms, the rate on its narrower pool would be 0.001417 / (0.53 x 0.60) = 0.0045. A label defined by insomnia also gives prescribers a clear patient type, and J&J sells Spravato and Caplyta to the same prescribers. 2024 was also Auvelity's second full year, not its peak. The case for lower: a mixed Phase 3 record, a failed head-to-head against generic quetiapine XR, and near-free generic sleep aids (trazodone, mirtazapine) already used for insomnia in depression. The Auvelity Medicare-diagnosed pool is broader than MDD (it includes dysthymia and other depressive disorders), and the rate is applied to an all-payer US pool
